text: dsh-agnes-image 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的图片与视频创作插件。它注册两个 agent 工具，并在侧边栏提供图片、视频、素材库和设置页面，可通过 Agnes 服务生成图片与视频、优化创作提示词、查看本地生成记录并打开文件。视频支持文字、首尾帧和参考素材模式，图片支持尺寸、比例及参考图。适合希望在 DSH 会话中直接创作视觉素材的用户；使用 Agnes 功能前需在设置面板填写 API Key。

dsh-agnes-image adds image and video generation to the DSH web client with two agent tools and a sidebar for creating and browsing media. It supports prompt refinement and text, keyframe, or reference video modes. Agnes features require an API key saved in panel settings.

dsh-agnes-image 的功能「生成图片」：根据提示词生成图片，可设置尺寸、画幅、数量并提供参考图。可从 agent 工具调用或侧边栏提交，生成文件保存到本地工作区。
dsh-agnes-image 的功能「生成视频」：按文字、首尾帧或参考素材提交视频任务，并等待任务完成后保存视频。可由 agent 工具或面板发起。
dsh-agnes-image 的功能「提示词优化」：将图片或视频提示词交给 Agnes 文本模型或 DSH 当前模型改写，用户可预览后采用、重试或放弃结果。
dsh-agnes-image 的功能「本地素材库」：浏览已记录的生成图片和视频历史，并对历史文件执行打开或删除等操作。
dsh-agnes-image 使用 Agnes 后端生成媒体或通过 Agnes 优化提示词时，会向 api.agnes-ai.cn 发送提示词及相关生成参数；使用这些功能需在面板设置中保存 Agnes API Key。

> **DeepSeek Harness can draw — and now it can move.** 4K stills, 4–12 s 720P video, a one-click prompt optimizer, a library that hands files to your desktop. Video runs on Agnes's free queue (¥0/s today); when the queue is busy the plugin backs off and retries instead of failing.

dsh-agnes-image README · or：dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add dsh-agnes-image
```

Agnes image and video generation for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-harness). It adds two agent tools (`agnes_generate_image`, `agnes_generate_video`), an AI prompt optimizer, and a sidebar panel with four tabs: Images, Videos, Library, Settings. Progress reporting is honest, cards are poster-first, and files are handed off to the desktop.

dsh-agnes-image README · or：The plugin ships without an API key. Install it, open the panel's Settings tab, paste your Agnes key once and save. Only then do the generation buttons light up; until then they are disabled and explain why. Credentials live in your own `%DSH_HOME%` data directory, never in this repository.

Both halves are hand-written against the official DSH bundle format. There is no build step: `index.js` is the host half, and `client.js` is the browser bundle.

Agnes APIs used:

| Image generation | `agnes-image-2.5-flash` | `POST https://api.agnes-ai.cn/v1/images/generations` |

| Prompt optimization | `agnes-3.0-flash` | `POST https://api.agnes-ai.cn/v1/chat/completions` |

dsh-agnes-image README · 1. Agent tool `agnes_generate_image`：Call it straight from a conversation.

Parameters: `prompt` (required), `size` (`1K`/`2K`/`3K`/`4K`), `ratio` (`1:1`, `3:4`, `4:3`, `16:9`, `9:16`, `2:3`, `3:2`, `21:9`), `count` (1–4), `reference_images` (image-to-image or composition: a public HTTPS URL or a `data:image/...;base64` string).

It returns absolute paths on disk, for example:

dsh-agnes-image README · 1. Agent tool `agnes_generate_image`：```
Agnes generated 1 image (agnes-image-2.5-flash, 2K 1:1).
Saved to disk — absolute paths:
  C:\...\default-workspace\agnes-images\2026-10-16\190212-测试：一只戴宇航头盔的柴犬.png  (836.9 KB)
```

dsh-agnes-image README · 2. Agent tool `agnes_generate_video`：This one blocks: create task, poll, download. The default ceiling is 15 minutes.

Parameters: `prompt` (required), `mode` (`text` / `keyframe` / `reference`), `seconds` (`"4"`–`"12"`, default `"5"`), `size` (`720P`; with `agnes-video-2.5` also `1080P`/`1K`/`2K`), `aspect_ratio` (`16:9`/`9:16`/`1:1`/`4:3`/`3:4`/`21:9`), `first_frame` / `last_frame` (keyframe mode), `images[]` / `audios[]` (reference mode), `seed`.

dsh-agnes-image README · 2. Agent tool `agnes_generate_video`：Agnes enforces the per-mode media rules, and this plugin validates them locally before the request, then re-throws the upstream error verbatim. `text` carries no media. `keyframe` needs at least one frame and no images or audios. `reference` needs at least one image or audio clip and no first or last frame. In `reference` mode local file paths are inlined into `data:` URLs automatically: single file under 15 MB, edge length 256–5760 px, and anything outside that errors. Public HTTPS URLs are accepted too.

dsh-agnes-image README · 3. AI prompt optimizer：Both prompt boxes, image and video, have an AI Optimize button. It hands the current prompt to a language model and shows a rewrite card first. The card holds only the rewritten prompt, expanded in place right under the prompt box and above the button. The original stays in the input above, the card does not repeat it, and it has no card title. Adopt writes it back, Discard throws it away, Retry asks again. The rewrite keeps subject and intent and only adds visual detail: composition, light, palette, material, mood, style. It follows the input language. The video side additionally asks for motion, camera movement and pacing.

dsh-agnes-image README · 3. AI prompt optimizer：Two backends, picked from a dropdown and persisted to settings:

| Backend | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `agnes` (default) | `agnes-3.0-flash` via Agnes Chat Completions, same key as generation |
| `dsh` | Reuses the harness' current conversation model (`agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()`). If the host has no LLM service or the profile has no model configured, the option shows as unavailable and nothing else is affected |
dsh-agnes-image README · 4. Sidebar panel：Four tabs, left to right: Images, Videos, Library, Settings. The panel shares the same host code path as the tools, so behavior is identical.

dsh-agnes-image README · 4. Sidebar panel：- Images: prompt, size, ratio, count, optional reference images. Thumbnails appear immediately.
- Videos: prompt, mode, seconds, aspect ratio, resolution. Keyframe mode reveals first/last frame inputs, reference mode reveals image and audio rows. After submit the button area shows queue and render progress and polls automatically. On completion it never plays in the panel; it shows a poster plus "Open with default app". History is not on this tab. Everything is collected in the Library.
- Progress bar: a running image job shows an indeterminate striped bar plus elapsed seconds. Image generation is a single call with no percentage, so no number is invented. A running video job shows the real upstream percentage (0/10/70/100), plus status and elapsed seconds, for example `Rendering: in_progress · 10% · 84s elapsed`. When the upstream percentage has not moved for more than 12 seconds, which is very common because the 10% step alone can sit for two minutes, the bar switches from a fill to flowing stripes and the caption becomes `Upstream still reports 10% — rendering · 132s elapsed`. It says where the number comes from instead of faking motion

dsh-agnes-image README · 4. Sidebar panel：Output layout:

- Images `<workspace>/agnes-images/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-<prompt slug>.<ext>`
- Videos `<workspace>/agnes-videos/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-<prompt slug>.mp4`
- Video poster `<same dir>/<same stem>-cover.png`, produced by the panel's frame grab

Repeated names within the same second get `-2`, `-3`. CJK prompts are preserved as-is.

The left variant only changes `animation-name` via `.is-left`; duration and curve are shared. |

No DOM measurement and no ResizeObserver, so it stays aligned when the sidebar is resized. |
| Library segmented switch | Same feel: body slides, pill slides | The key includes `libraryKind`, so direction follows the switch. It reuses the same `pillStyle()`. |
| Card expand / collapse | 200 ms true-height transition | The expanded area stays in the DOM, so its hei

dsh-agnes-image README · Interaction & motion：Horizontal overflow from the slide is clipped at the panel root with `overflow-x:hidden`, otherwise a horizontal scrollbar appears mid-animation. The pill is already in place on first render, so opening the panel never shows it sliding in from the first tab.

dsh-agnes-image README · Interaction & motion：Tab switching only animates `transform`, never `opacity`. The tab body remounts, and starting from `opacity:0` made tall form tabs flash the bare dark panel background for about 100 ms before growing in, which was far more jarring than the animation itself. It is fully opaque from frame one, direction comes from the 40 px offset alone, and there is no gap.

dsh-agnes-image README · Interaction & motion：The collapsed expand area stays in the DOM but is neither focusable nor clickable. `CardShell` uses a `ref` + `useEffect` to set `inert` on the container while collapsed and remove it when expanded. That is the DOM API rather than a JSX prop, so React 18 and 19 behave the same.

dsh-agnes-image README · Key policy: panel only, no shipped credential：The only source is the key saved in the panel's Settings tab, written to `%DSH_HOME%\agnes-image\settings.json`.

`Config` has no `apiKey` field and there is no environment-variable fallback. The plaintext key row and `apiKeyEnv` that early versions had are gone. `resolveKey()` reads the settings panel only. Without a key, `status.hasKey === false` and `keySource === 'none'`, and every generation or optimize call on the agnes backend fails with:
section: Key policy: panel only, no shipped credential

dsh-agnes-image README · Key policy: panel only, no shipped credential：`No Agnes API key configured: open the panel Settings tab and save one first (the plugin ships without a key).`

The reasoning: plugins get distributed and copied around, so a credential may only ever live in the user's own data directory, never inside plugin source. `status` reports just `keySource` (`panel` / `none`) and a masked `keyHint` holding the first six and last four characters. It never reports the full key.

dsh-agnes-image README · HTTP routes：Routes are registered through `ctx.connection.fetch.register`, so the `/api` prefix gets authentication automatically. Do not switch to `ctx.webServer.register`, which bypasses it.

dsh-agnes-image README · `/open` safety boundary：`open` only opens paths recorded in history, meaning the `file` field of `history.json` or `video-history.json`. Anything else returns 404 `no history record for that file`, otherwise the route would be a generic "open any local file" channel for the page. The host also `stat`s the file to confirm it is still there, and first asks `canOpenNativePath()`. A host without a desktop session, meaning headless, answers `this host cannot open local files (<platform>)`. Calls carry a 30-second timeout.

dsh-agnes-image README · Pitfall: `requestBody` is required, even on GET routes：`ConnectionFetchRoute.requestBody` is typed `'buffered' | 'streaming'` (`ConnectionRequestBodyMode`), and there is no "absent" member. `createSharedFetchHandler`'s `requestBodyMode` returns it unchanged (`dsh-client-connection/lib/index.js:610-613`). The HTTP bridge, in the same file at `:43-81`, only special-cases `bodyMode === "buffered"`. Every other value takes the streaming branch, which builds a Request with a body via `Readable.toWeb(req)`. That is illegal for GET and HEAD, so `new Request(url, { method: 'GET', body })` throws before any response exists, and the browser only sees 400 with an empty body and no content-type.
section: Pitfall: `requestBody` is required, even on GET routes

text: dsh-agnes-image README · Pitfall: `requestBody` is required, even on GET routes：So every route here declares `requestBody: 'buffered'`, including the GET routes. `run.mjs` carries regression assertions for this (`requestBody declared …` / `bridge accepts …`), so a route edit cannot silently drop it.
section: Pitfall: `requestBody` is required, even on GET routes

text:
dsh-agnes-image README · Video upstream rate limits (measured)：- `POST /v1/videos` frequently answers 429 (`rate_limit_exceeded`) or 503 `video_queue_full` on the free tier. This plugin retries 429/500/502/503/504 with exponential backoff, default `videoQueueRetries: 6` and delay `min(30s, 5s × attempt)`.
- Polling also eats 429s. `GET /agnesapi` interleaves 429s in practice, so polling treats 429/5xx/network errors as retryable, reports `pending` and keeps waiting. It never marks the task failed, otherwise a perfectly healthy render would be reported as broken.
- Three failure envelopes exist: `{"detail":…}`, `{"code":…,"message":…}` and `{"error":{"message":…}}`. `videoErrorText()` recognizes all three.
- `agnes-video-2.5-flash` supports `"720P"` only. Any other `size` is normalized to `720P` locally; upstream returns a hard 400 `size must be 720P` for flash.
- `id`, `task_id` and `video_id` are the same task string in the create response. Polling uses `video_id`.

dsh-agnes-image README · Prompt optimization: two backends and their limits：- The agnes backend uses `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `temperature: 0.7` and `max_tokens` set to Config `optimizeMaxTokens`, default 900. It retries 429/500/502/503/504 up to 3 times at `2000 ms × attempt`, and shares the same envelope parser as image and video.
- The dsh backend uses `ctx.llm.stream({ provider, model, messages, system, maxTokens, sessionId, purpose, signal })`, with provider and model from `ctx.get('agentDefaultModel')?.currentSelection()`, the same usage as the core `dsh-session-title-llm` package. A `BlockAssembler` collects the stream. Only `finish.kind === 'stop'` counts as success; `tool-call` and `max-tokens` are reported as failures.
- `inject` deliberately omits `llm`. A missing LLM service only disables the "DSH current model" optimizer option, and `status.llmAvailable` / `llmRoute` report it honestly, instead of leaving the whole plugin pending and taking image and video generation down with it.
- Input is capped at 4000 characters. Over that you get `prompt is too long to optimize (4000 characters max)`. The output strips ``` fences, `优化结果：`-style prefixes and paired quotes,
section: Prompt optimization: two backends and their limits

text: dsh-agnes-image README · Panel CTA colors：Primary buttons (Generate / Generate video / Save) use a fixed fill of `#ff7700` with dark ink text `#1f1300` for contrast, about 8:1. White on orange is only about 2.7:1. Hover `#e86b00`, active `#d96100` and the `:focus-visible` ring come from a `<style>` injected by `apply()`, with class `.dsh-agnes-primary` and idempotent dedup via `data-plugin-css="dsh-agnes-image/button.css"`, mirroring the core `dsh-client-ui-message-feedback/lib/client.js:12-20` approach. Inline styles cannot express `:hover`. The fill is also written inline so the button stays orange even if injection is blocked. The same stylesheet carries the progress-bar classes `.dsh-agnes-bar`: track `--dsw-alias-bg-layer-2`, fill `#ff7700`, indeterminate state animated by `@keyframes dsh-agnes-bar-slide` and degrading to a static bar under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Everything else uses `--dsw-alias-*` / `--dsw-static-*` theme tokens only.

dsh-agnes-image README · Known limitations：- Tool results cannot render as inline image or video cards. The web client only renders image cards for the built-in `read_image`, and third-party `presentResult` is not consumed. Both tools therefore return local paths. To see an image in the chat, send `@<path>` or hand the path to `read_image`. The panel displays thumbnails and posters through the core route `api/file?path=<absolute path>`. Videos only offer "open with default app" when expanded, never in-panel playback.
- "Insert into composer" writes plain text: `` for images and `[name](absolute path)` for videos. DSH exposes no public API to attach media to the composer, so it is text, not an attachment.
- The video tool is blocking. `text` mode takes about 3 minutes and up, with progress sitting at 10 for a long time, and its `timeoutMs` is 900000. The panel uses the non-blocking `video-create` + `video-status` routes, so closing the page does not affect the task; the host resumes from the task table.
- Video reference limits come from upstream. Flash accepts ≤ 5 images and ≤ 3 audio clips, under 15 MB per file. Inlining local files as `data:` URLs also bounds the request body.

dsh-agnes-image README · Development verification：The author's harness (`run.mjs`) loads both halves against the real `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` + `schemastery` and checks: both tools and all twelve routes registering, the `requestBody` contract and bridge compatibility, Config defaults including video and optimizer plus "Config carries no credential", two real generations written to disk, history, the panel-only key policy (with no key, all three entry points must refuse: status, routes and tools; after saving, `keySource: 'panel'`; after clearing, `none` rather than falling back to Config), settings persistence, the `/open` refusal paths (missing `file` → 400, unrecorded path → 404; the success path is deliberately untested because it would really launch a desktop app), the full `/video-cover` chain (unrecorded → 404, non-PNG data URL → 400, empty frame → 400, and a success path over a fake MP4 plus a planted history row → 200, PNG on disk, `cover` filled in history), delete safety, video parameter validation (mode/media/unknown task), prompt optimization (empty/too long/DSH backend unavailable/real Agnes rewrites for both image and video prompts), the client slot and dictionary co

dsh-agnes-image README · Development verification：It also runs without a key. When no key is found, the real-upstream sections (tool calls, panel generation, prompt optimization, and `video-create` payload validation, which resolves the key before validating) are marked `SKIP` and the rest continues. An offline run yields 92 PASS / 0 FAIL with 6 sections skipped, while a run with a key in the panel executes everything and has measured 124 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 SKIP, including real generation and disk output, delete, poster capture, both prompt rewrites, the 99-key dictionaries and the 8 motion assertions.
